design.title: Metric cabinet-frame diffusion with a world-context bypass
design.coverage_gap: The exact N=2 support has one LL and one HH episode. Cabinet x and yaw are confounded, and neither crossed cells nor yaw magnitudes of 33--37 degrees are observed. Per-coordinate support standardization would particularly magnify the almost-constant goal y and yaw cosine outside support.
design.reusable_regularity: A translating drawer is approached relative to its handle and pulled along its cabinet axis. Analytically express hand-handle separation, goal-handle remaining displacement, and observed hand/handle increments in the cabinet yaw basis; diffuse actions in that same orthonormal basis. Fixed metric scales and an additional smooth near-contact view do not identify a demonstration or fit an extrapolation trend from two layouts. This candidate has no learned preprocessing and no auxiliary objective.
dependencies_preserved: The frame is a coordinate change, not a claim of full environment rotation invariance: retain absolute world hand and goal coordinates, world vertical, yaw sine/cosine, and both handle quaternions for fixed robot orientation/workspace and cabinet contact geometry.
Current hand and handle positions, gripper aperture, and native previous hand/handle/aperture encode contact alignment and observed motion. Two whole observation histories are processed separately.

All real positional fields are reconstructible from the unbounded relation vectors and world hand/goal bypass. Current and previous quaternions are unmodified. Absent object2 fields are omitted as declared by task_materials.json.

The cabinet is the relevant visible obstacle. Handle position, cabinet yaw, and remaining drawer travel retain its task-varying geometry; no collision-free path or simulator field is supplied or inferred.

evidence_refs.detail: Two complete current-support episodes, images_and_numeric, no development/test data.
Yaw-corrected handle point, yaw channels 39:41, fixed end-effector rotation, world delta controls, LL/HH training versus crossed and extreme layouts.
178 transitions; initial handle-goal distances approximately 0.128 m in both demos; goal-y std approximately 0.000708 and yaw-cosine std approximately 0.002376.
Cabinet, handle, fixed-orientation fingers and initial offset are visible.
Raised approach above the handle, rather than immediate straight-line pulling.
Raised approach in the opposite signed layout.
Read actions 0:28 and 40:72, observations 21:26 and 62:70: vertical action reverses around 23; pulling starts near 65 after a close descent.
Read observations 63:68: similar final descent with opposite-signed layout geometry.

expected_failure_signature: If local-coordinate transfer is sufficient, new layouts should preserve approach and pull direction; if the world bypass becomes a layout identifier, crossed-cell actions will instead follow the wrong lateral direction.
At extreme yaw the fixed gripper can lose contact despite correct local translation. That would appear as hand motion along the desired pull axis without matching handle travel.
No explicit stage supervision: diffusion can switch to descent/pull prematurely after off-support approach errors, especially with four-step open-loop execution.

required_runtime_fields.fields: hand 0:3; aperture 3:4; handle 4:7; quaternion 7:11; previous hand 18:21; previous aperture 21:22; previous handle 22:25; previous quaternion 25:29; goal 36:39; cabinet sin/cos yaw 39:41
39:41 only for the fixed chunk action basis

design.action_frame_semantics: For every one of 16 native action4 rows, encode xyz as Rz(yaw_start)^T times the unitless world displacement command; decode by Rz(yaw_start). Z and gripper are unchanged. No translation of action points, rescaling, candidate clipping, changing native 0.01 m scale, or future frame use. Host alone clips the world cube and executes four actions.
design.support_fit_statistics: None. Raw-history physical scaling is a representation choice; the common normalizer remains untouched. Its standardized history is not used by this design.
design.architecture: Exactly one common DP factory call, condition_dim=33, diffusion_action_dim=4. All learned capacity belongs to the frozen common U-Net. Common mask-normalized action epsilon objective only.
change_summary: Initial executable design: analytical yaw canonicalization, metric relation and increment features, near-contact tanh features, and world-context bypass. No performance feedback used.
